processing: Sun-dried sheng maocha from tall, undwarfed old trees, kept loose or pressed, with no ripe-style fermentation.
harvest_season: Spring is the prized picking, as elsewhere in Yiwu.
appearance_dry: Tight, handsome, largely whole dark-green strands.
taste_profile: Described as densely honey-scented and long, with a lasting sweet return and a fragrance that stays in the empty cup.

brewing.notes: As with other Yiwu teas, full heat brings out the fragrance; long early steeps are not needed.

vintage_note: Sold by harvest year, like other sheng, mostly young spring old-tree tea from small makers. It is a lesser-known village name, so wrappers may simply say Yiwu. Gaoshan also appears as a name in the Manzhuan area, so ask which is meant.
description:
Gaoshanzhai, or Gaoshan village, is an Yi community in the Yiwu tea area of Mengla County. Its name simply means high mountain village, which is why you need to be a bit careful: a Gaoshan Zhai is also listed under Manzhuan.

Its selling point is the trees. They have not been cut down to picking height, so they stand tall and pickers have to climb, and villagers are said to look after them closely. Processing by the Yi growers is reported to have improved in recent years.

The cup is described as Yiwu in its sweeter, honeyed mode, with a golden liquor and a long finish. That description comes from tea writing, not any wide record, so take it as a starting point.

Ask for the village and the year.
history: Little is documented about the village's early tea history. Its reputation has grown only in recent years.
